rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a representative multimodal configuration. config_002 uses PCA and ViT encoders with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which are common choices that balance complexity and performance. This clarifies the baseline performance of a standard multimodal setup, providing critical initial data for subsequent exploration.

The existing evidence shows that the previous configuration (config_002) achieved 0.5856 validation accuracy using pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 and switching fusion to concat, which could clarify if these changes improve performance. It balances exploration of image encoder alternatives and fusion methods while maintaining similar RNA and aggregation choices, providing critical insights without repeating prior configurations.

The existing evidence shows config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.5856). This experiment tests a similar configuration but replaces the RNA encoder with scvi_n200, which may improve performance. It clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice (pca_n2000 vs scvi_n200) significantly impacts accuracy, while maintaining the promising multimodal setup and fusion/aggregation methods from the current best.

Existing evidence shows config_014 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests scvi_n200 + resnet50 with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, exploring if the image encoder choice (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) impacts performance. It balances exploitation of the current best RNA encoder with exploration of a different image encoder, which could yield higher accuracy or clarify the importance of the image encoder.

Existing evidence shows config_014 (scVI_n200 + ViT-L + Transformer + weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders and aggregation method but with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion. It clarifies whether the fusion method is a critical factor, balancing exploitation of the top-performing configuration with exploration of alternative design choices.

Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation achieves higher accuracy (config_014: 0.725) than avgpool (config_032: 0.713). This experiment tests whether using transformer aggregation with resnet50 image encoder (instead of imagenet_vit_l) maintains high performance, clarifying if image encoder choice is critical. It exploits the promising scvi_n200 foundation while exploring aggregation method consistency across image encoders.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_014) achieve high accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and fusion settings (transformer + weighted), exploring whether a different RNA encoder could improve performance. It balances exploitation of proven components (imagenet_vit_l, transformer) with exploration of RNA encoder alternatives, prioritizing high-impact design choices.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_014) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with the same image encoder and transformer aggregation but concat fusion, clarifying if RNA encoder choice or fusion method has a greater impact. It balances exploration of RNA encoder alternatives while leveraging proven image encoder and aggregation settings.

The existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_014) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA with resnet50 image encoder and avgpool aggregation, which could clarify whether avgpool aggregation improves performance compared to transformer aggregation. This balances exploitation of the scvi_n200 RNA encoder (a high-performing component) with exploration of alternative aggregation methods, maximizing the chance of finding a better configuration within the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_014) achieve high accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests changing aggregation from transformer to avgpool while keeping weighted fusion, which could clarify if avgpool aggregation improves performance. It directly builds on the top-performing architecture, balancing exploitation of proven components with a critical parameter change.
